headword: {連立政権|れんりつせいけん}

definitions.explanation: a government formed by two or more political parties working together, typically when no single party has enough seats to govern alone

examples.japanese: {連立政権|れんりつせいけん}が{発足|ほっそく}した。
{連立政権|れんりつせいけん}は{政策|せいさく}の{一致|いっち}が{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: It's difficult for a coalition government to agree on policy.

examples.japanese: {与党|よとう}は{過半数|かはんすう}を{取|と}れなかったため、{他党|たとう}と{連立政権|れんりつせいけん}を{組|く}むことになった。
examples.english: Since the ruling party failed to win a majority, it had to form a coalition government with other parties.

notes:
Combines {連立|れんりつ} (coalition, alliance) and {政権|せいけん} (political power, government). Japan has had multiple coalition governments, most notably the long-running LDP-Komeito coalition. The term is a staple of political news coverage.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {連立政権|れんりつせいけん}を{組|く}む: to form a coalition government
- {連立政権|れんりつせいけん}が{崩壊|ほうかい}する: for a coalition government to collapse
- {連立政権|れんりつせいけん}の{維持|いじ}: maintenance of a coalition government
- {連立政権|れんりつせいけん}の{枠組|わくぐ}み: framework of a coalition government

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {単独政権|たんどくせいけん}: single-party government — a government formed by one party alone
- {連立与党|れんりつよとう}: coalition ruling parties — the parties that make up the coalition
- {政権交代|せいけんこうたい}: change of government — when power shifts from one party or coalition to another
